nodes.label: extend_ttl
nodes.rationale: extend_ttl(threshold, extend_to) is a no-op unless the current TTL is below the threshold, then it sets TTL to extend_to. It is idempotent and never shortens. Extending on every write, so active users pay for their own state, is the standard per-user pattern. Extending instance TTL at busy entry points keeps globals alive. Rent is charged at invocation time.

nodes.label: extend_ttl_with_limits
nodes.rationale: Protocol 26 added extend_ttl_with_limits for persistent and instance storage so callers cannot force arbitrary rent costs. It takes extend_to, min_extension, and max_extension.

nodes.label: ExtendFootprintTTLOp
nodes.rationale: Anyone can extend any entry's TTL with ExtendFootprintTTLOp and no contract authorization. Benevolent keep-alive services are possible, which is why expiry cannot enforce a permission deadline.

nodes.label: Instance Storage
nodes.rationale: Instance storage shares one TTL with the contract instance, so one extend_ttl warms every global. It is capped at the network max entry size (64KB serialized on mainnet). Never put per-user or unbounded data there. Use it for an admin address, config, and other small global state.

nodes.label: Persistent Storage
nodes.rationale: Persistent entries have a per-key TTL. When they expire they are archived, not deleted, and can be restored. Use them for user balances and anything that must survive being untouched.

nodes.label: Storage
nodes.rationale: Instance, persistent, and temporary storage have different lifetimes and costs. Choosing the wrong type is a top source of bugs and fee waste. Contract state lives in storage, never in the #[contract] struct.

nodes.label: Temporary Storage
nodes.rationale: Temporary entries have a per-key TTL and are deleted permanently when they expire. They are the cheapest fit for caches, time-bounded data, and oracle prices. There is no restore path.

nodes.label: Token Allowances
nodes.rationale: approve(from, spender, amount, expiration_ledger) expires. The convention is temporary storage keyed by (from, spender) with a TTL matching the expiration. Re-approving overwrites, so a spender can front-run a reduction and spend the old amount plus the new one. Mitigate by approving to 0 first or by using exact-amount auth instead of a standing allowance.

nodes.label: TTL
nodes.rationale: TTL is counted in ledgers, about 5 seconds each and 17280 per day. On mainnet, new persistent entries start near 120 days, temporary entries near 1 day, and no entry can exceed about 180 days. Since protocol 23, archived persistent entries in the read-write footprint are restored automatically and rent is paid again. Temporary expiry means deleted. TTL expiry is not a security mechanism: if data must become invalid after a deadline, store the deadline in the value and check it. Code should not assume a previously written entry is still present.

nodes.label: extend_ttl
nodes.rationale: extend_ttl(threshold, extend_to) keeps instance state from being archived.

nodes.label: Check-then-act Races
nodes.rationale: State can change between transactions, so checks and state changes must be atomic in one invocation, and swaps should take a caller-supplied min_out. approve overwrites, so reducing a non-zero allowance can be front-run; approve to 0 first or use exact-amount auth.

nodes.label: TTL and Archival Failures
nodes.rationale: A temporary entry can disappear permanently, and a persistent entry can archive and add restoration friction. Separately, anyone can extend any entry via ExtendFootprintTTLOp, so expiry is not a permission boundary. Store an explicit deadline in the value and check it.

nodes.label: ANR
nodes.rationale: ANRs come from main-thread blocking in native code, including synchronous I/O in native modules. Low-end Android, about 3GB of RAM or less, is the real target. Persist in-progress forms and transactions because the process can be killed.

nodes.label: expo-image
nodes.rationale: Use disk and memory cache, contentFit, and blurhash or thumbhash placeholders, and always pass width and height. Decoded bitmap memory is about width times height times 4 bytes, so a 4000 by 3000 photo is about 48MB. Prefetch only what is about to show. Prefer WebP or AVIF.

nodes.label: JSI

nodes.label: Memory
nodes.rationale: Images and long lists dominate. Bound caches with an LRU, do not keep large blobs or full history in React state, lower windowSize, and size images correctly. Cancel in-flight requests and do not setState after unmount.

nodes.label: JS thread
nodes.rationale: Low JS FPS means the JS thread is the bottleneck. Avoid large JSON parse or stringify, big array spreads, cascading setState from sockets, and console.log on hot paths. Batch network results into one state update, debounce search, and throttle scroll handlers.

nodes.label: UI thread
nodes.rationale: Low UI FPS means native or draw work. Heavy row content such as SVG, QR codes, gradients, and shadows is the usual cost. Use lightweight placeholders or cache them as images. Use elevation sparingly because shadows overdraw. Avoid stacked translucent layers.

nodes.label: JS thread

nodes.label: UI thread
nodes.rationale: UI-thread bottlenecks are overdraw, huge views, shadows, non-native animations, and big images. The frame budget is about 16ms at 60fps or 8ms at 120fps.

nodes.label: Release Profile
nodes.rationale: opt-level z, overflow-checks, strip symbols, panic abort, codegen-units 1, and lto keep the release WASM small.

nodes.label: __constructor
nodes.rationale: Prefer __constructor over a separate initialize function because it removes the front-running window between deploy and init. The name must be exact, it runs only at creation, failure aborts deployment atomically, and a contract deployed without a constructor cannot gain one later.

nodes.label: Deployer
nodes.rationale: env.deployer() updates the current contract WASM and deploys new instances. with_address(current contract, salt) plus deploy_v2(wasm_hash, constructor_args) is the factory path.

nodes.label: Factories
nodes.rationale: Factory addresses are deterministic per deployer and salt. deployed_address computes one without deploying. Authorize who may deploy, emit an event per deployment so instances are indexable, and keep factory logic separate from instance business logic.

nodes.label: i128
nodes.rationale: i128 is the canonical SEP-41 token amount and admits negatives, so inputs must reject amount < 0.

nodes.label: OpenZeppelin stellar-contracts

nodes.label: SEP-0049
nodes.rationale: SEP-0049 standardizes upgradeable-contract interfaces.

nodes.label: U256 and I256
nodes.rationale: U256 and I256 are the 256-bit types. Their checked arithmetic methods return Option and require protocol 26 or later.

nodes.label: Upgradeability
nodes.rationale: Decide early whether the contract is mutable. Gate upgrade behind admin or governance auth. Upload the new WASM first and pass its hash to update_current_contract_wasm. The address and all storage survive; only the executable changes, and __constructor does not re-run. Storage schema is the contract's problem: reading an old key with a changed contracttype shape fails to decode. Store a schema version, add enum variants rather than reshaping them, and ship an idempotent admin-gated migrate that requires new_version > current_version.

nodes.label: Scout
nodes.rationale: CoinFabrik Scout (cargo scout-audit) ships 20+ detectors, including missing overflow checks, unprotected WASM update, unrestricted transfers, unsafe unwrap, and DoS-unbounded ops, and can emit SARIF for CI.

nodes.label: __constructor
nodes.rationale: __constructor runs once, atomically, at deploy time, and does not run again on upgrade.

nodes.label: stellar contract upload

nodes.label: Integer Overflow
nodes.rationale: overflow-checks = true panics on overflow in the release profile, but explicit checked math fails cleaner and survives a profile mistake. An unchecked negative i128 transfer withdraws from the recipient. Use checked methods for 256-bit types on protocol 26 and later.

nodes.label: Reinitialization Attacks
nodes.rationale: A guarded initialize matters only when you do not use __constructor, which cannot re-run. Without a check-and-set flag, anyone can call initialize and capture admin.

nodes.label: CAP-71 Auth Delegation
nodes.rationale: Protocol 27 lets __check_auth read get_delegated_signers (unsanitized transaction input; check that each address is a registered delegate) and call delegate_auth to forward the check to a G- or C-address. Delegation can nest, so modular accounts do not need a separate auth entry per delegate.

nodes.label: __check_auth
nodes.rationale: A contract account (smart wallet, multisig, or passkey) implements CustomAccountInterface. The host calls __check_auth with the signature payload hash, a contracttype signature, and auth contexts. Always verify signature_payload itself. Use auth_contexts for spend limits and allowlists. Never require_auth the account's own address inside __check_auth. Keep it lean; its cost is added to every transaction the account signs. ed25519_verify is the usual signature check.

nodes.label: Resource Limits
nodes.rationale: Transactions pay an inclusion fee plus a resource fee for declared CPU, ledger reads and writes, transaction size, events, and rent. Rent and events are refunded if unused; instructions and I/O are charged as declared, so simulate first and leave headroom when state can diverge from simulation. Mainnet ceilings at time of writing include 400M CPU instructions, 40 MB memory, 200 entries read and 200 written, 200 KB read and about 129 KB written, about 129 KB transaction size, 16 KB events plus return value, 128 KB WASM, and 64 KB per ledger entry (keys 250 bytes). Limits change by validator vote.

nodes.label: __check_auth Pitfalls
nodes.rationale: Verify signature_payload itself. Enforce policy from auth_contexts, or a policy wallet is decorative. CAP-71 get_delegated_signers is unsanitized: verify each address is a registered delegate before delegate_auth.

nodes.label: Fee Griefing
nodes.rationale: If worst-case cost on attacker-shaped input exceeds network limits, legitimate users are denied service. Cap loops over user-controlled collections, per-iteration storage or events, and signature counts in __check_auth. Keep footprints small.

nodes.label: Scout
nodes.rationale: CoinFabrik cargo scout-audit: 20+ detectors, including missing overflow checks, unprotected WASM update, unrestricted transfers, unsafe unwrap, and unbounded-operation denial of service. SARIF output for CI.

nodes.label: Network Limits
nodes.rationale: Numeric limits quoted in the skill are mainnet settings at time of writing and change by validator vote. Stellar Lab's Network Limits page and stellar network settings --network mainnet show the live values.

nodes.label: Ledger Time in Tests

nodes.label: Test Resource Limits

nodes.label: Resource Profiling

nodes.label: Governance Timelock
nodes.rationale: For upgrades and config changes, propose stores the action and an execute-after ledger, execute enforces the delay, and cancel lets governance abort. Separate proposer, approver, and executor for multisig, store proposals in persistent storage, and block replay with unique ids, expiry, and events. A custom account is often cleaner than in-contract multisig for signature-set policies.

nodes.label: Contract Factory
nodes.rationale: deploy_v2 with with_address(current contract, salt) makes the address deterministic per deployer and salt. deployed_address computes it without deploying. Authorize deployers, emit an event per deployment, and keep factory logic out of instance logic.

nodes.label: panic_with_error!
nodes.rationale: panic_with_error!(&env, Error::X) surfaces a typed error. A bare panic becomes an opaque host error.

nodes.label: SEP-0049
nodes.rationale: SEP-0049 standardizes upgradeable-contract interfaces.

nodes.label: Reinitialization Attacks
nodes.rationale: Only matters for a guarded initialize instead of __constructor, which cannot re-run. Without a check-and-set flag, anyone can call initialize and capture admin.

nodes.label: __constructor
nodes.rationale: Runs once, atomically, at deploy time. The function must be named __constructor. It does not run again on upgrade.

nodes.label: stellar contract deploy
nodes.rationale: Constructor arguments are passed after the -- separator.

nodes.label: stellar contract upload
nodes.rationale: Uploads WASM without instantiating, for factories or upgrades. stellar contract install is a deprecated alias.

nodes.label: Fork Tests
nodes.rationale: stellar snapshot create writes ledger JSON, and Env::from_ledger_snapshot_file replays tests against it. For an upgrade rehearsal, stellar contract fetch pulls the deployed WASM so the old and new versions can be compared.

nodes.label: __constructor
nodes.rationale: Prefer __constructor over a separate initialize. It runs once, atomically, at creation and removes the front-running window between deploy and init. It does not run on upgrade. Failure aborts deployment. A contract deployed without a constructor cannot gain one later.

nodes.label: Contract Upgrade
nodes.rationale: If the contract is mutable, gate upgrade on admin or governance auth. Upload the new WASM first and pass its hash to deployer().update_current_contract_wasm. The address and storage survive; only the executable changes, and __constructor does not re-run. A changed #[contracttype] shape fails to decode. Store a schema version, add enum variants instead of reshaping keys, and ship an idempotent admin-gated migrate that requires new_version > current_version. contractmeta! can record binver.

nodes.label: CAP-71 Auth Delegation
nodes.rationale: Protocol 27 (CAP-71) lets a modular account delegate authentication inside __check_auth. get_delegated_signers returns unsanitized addresses supplied by the transaction, so the account must check that they are registered delegates before delegate_auth forwards the current check. Delegation can nest and does not need a separate auth entry per delegate.

nodes.label: __check_auth
nodes.rationale: The host calls __check_auth with a host-computed signature_payload digest, the signature artifact, and auth_contexts for the calls this auth would cover. Always verify signature_payload itself; verifying any other message authorizes arbitrary calls. Use auth_contexts for spend limits and function allowlists. Never require_auth the account's own address inside __check_auth, because that function is evaluating auth rather than consuming it.

nodes.label: Custom Accounts
nodes.rationale: A contract address can act as an account, such as a smart wallet, multisig, or passkey wallet, by implementing CustomAccountInterface. Keep the check lean because its cost is added to every transaction the account signs.

nodes.label: Fees and Resource Limits
nodes.rationale: Contract transactions pay an inclusion fee plus a resource fee for CPU instructions, ledger reads and writes, transaction size, events size, and rent. Rent and events are refundable if unused; instructions and I/O are charged as declared, so submitters simulate first. If state diverges from simulation, costs can shift, so leave headroom. Quoted mainnet ceilings, including 400M CPU, 40MB memory, 200 reads and writes, 128KB WASM, and 64KB ledger entries, change by validator vote. Minimize distinct ledger entries, cap unbounded loops, and treat crypto verification inside __check_auth as the expensive primitive.

nodes.label: Read-Write Footprint
nodes.rationale: Every transaction declares its read/write footprint up front. Transactions that touch the same read-write entry serialize. Everything touched must be in the footprint whether or not it is used, and each entry has a fixed cost plus bytes.

nodes.label: Governance Timelock
nodes.rationale: For upgrades and config changes, prefer a timelock: propose stores the action and an execute-after ledger, execute enforces the delay, and cancel lets governance abort. For multisig, separate proposer, approver, and executor, store proposals in persistent storage, and prevent replay with unique IDs, expiry, and explicit events. A custom account is often cleaner than in-contract multisig.

nodes.label: Typed Storage Keys
nodes.rationale: A #[contracttype] key enum centralizes the schema and prevents collisions. Adding variants is the forward-compatible way to grow storage. Fine-grained keys let unrelated transactions run in parallel; one giant Map serializes callers and makes every caller pay to read all of it.

nodes.label: Ledger Test State
nodes.rationale: env.ledger().set_timestamp and set_sequence_number advance ledger time so vesting and timelock logic can be tested without waiting for ledgers.

nodes.label: Custom Account Pitfalls
nodes.rationale: Verify signature_payload itself. Enforce policies from auth_contexts; ignoring them makes a policy wallet decorative. CAP-71 get_delegated_signers returns unsanitized user input, so verify each address is a registered delegate before delegate_auth.

nodes.label: Resource Exhaustion
nodes.rationale: A function whose worst-case cost on attacker-shaped input exceeds network limits denies service to legitimate users. Cap loops over user-controlled collections, per-iteration storage or events, and signature counts in __check_auth, and keep footprints small.

nodes.label: Storage Key Collisions
nodes.rationale: Untyped keys can silently overwrite unrelated data. Always use a #[contracttype] key enum.

nodes.label: MuxedAddress
nodes.rationale: MuxedAddress distinguishes sub-accounts of one address for exchanges and custodians. Token transfer accepts it as the destination, and a plain Address converts into it.

nodes.label: Stellar Asset Contract
nodes.rationale: Every classic Stellar asset, including native XLM, exposes SEP-41 through its SAC. G-account balances live in trustlines with a 64-bit cap, and a missing or unauthorized trustline fails the transfer. C-account balances live in contract storage at full i128. Issuer flags apply, including AUTH_REQUIRED, AUTH_REVOCABLE freezes, and clawback. Transfers to the issuer burn and transfers from the issuer mint. A protocol that accepts arbitrary token addresses must survive all of this. The SAC adds the SEP-0011 asset string as a trailing event topic.

nodes.label: SEP-41
nodes.rationale: SEP-41 is the token interface. transfer, approve, and burn authorize from; transfer_from and burn_from authorize the spender, because the allowance already authorized from. Reads need no auth. mint, clawback, set_admin, set_authorized, and trust are SAC admin surface, not SEP-41. Wallets and indexers depend on the standard transfer, approve, mint, burn, and clawback event shapes.

nodes.label: StellarAssetClient
nodes.rationale: StellarAssetClient is the SAC admin surface: mint, clawback, set_admin, set_authorized, and trust (protocol 26+). It is not the SEP-41 client.

nodes.label: TokenClient
nodes.rationale: The SDK ships TokenClient for anything that implements the standard token interface, including every Stellar asset through its SAC, so no WASM import is required.

nodes.label: Threat Model
nodes.rationale: Assume the attacker controls every function argument, transaction ordering and timing, every account that does not require a signature, contracts that mimic your interface, and the shape of on-chain state they can legally create, including entry counts and TTLs. They can even extend your entries' TTLs.

nodes.label: Token-consumer Review
nodes.rationale: Any contract that takes a token address must assume native XLM's SAC, a wrapped classic asset's SAC, or a custom contract. Permissionless tokens bring arbitrary-call risk. Do not assume 7 decimals. Re-check the received amount after transfer when fee-on-transfer tokens matter. Survive missing trustlines, AUTH_REQUIRED, frozen accounts, and issuer clawback. transfer_from must authorize the spender, not from, and standard token events must be emitted.

nodes.label: Arbitrary Contract Calls
nodes.rationale: A user-supplied contract address is arbitrary code. It can fail, trap, burn budget, emit misleading events, or call other contracts. It cannot re-enter you. Allowlist external contracts.

nodes.label: contracterror

nodes.label: Arbitrary Contract Calls

nodes.label: Env

nodes.label: Execution Model

The host meters every step. A transaction is the atomicity boundary: errors, panics, missing auth, and budget exhaustion roll back every ledger write, including nested calls. A caller can catch a callee error with try_ client methods and continue. Contract state lives in storage, never in the #[contract] struct.

nodes.label: authorize_as_current_contract
nodes.rationale: A direct call from contract A to B authorizes only B's immediate require_auth of A's address. If B will make a deeper call that needs A's auth, A must pre-authorize it with authorize_as_current_contract and an InvokerContractAuthEntry.

nodes.label: Medium Threshold
nodes.rationale: Stellar accounts satisfy contract authorization at their medium threshold.

nodes.label: require_auth
nodes.rationale: require_auth asks the host whether this address authorized this contract, this function, and these exact arguments. Require it when the call spends, reduces, reconfigures, or consumes that address's authority downstream. Reads and credits need no auth. Authorizing a caller-supplied who only proves control of who; load the privileged address from storage and authorize that.

nodes.label: require_auth_for_args
nodes.rationale: Narrows the signed payload to the arguments you pass, so a signer can commit to a maximum and the contract enforces actual <= max.

nodes.label: Auth Replay through Middleware
nodes.rationale: If a user pre-signed an auth tree that includes an inner token.transfer, anyone can call a wrapper that never authorizes that user and consume the signature. Re-authorize at every layer that uses an address's authority. This is the most common real-world auth bug.

nodes.label: Host Auth Replay Protection
nodes.rationale: Nonces and expirations on authorization entries are enforced by the host, not by contract code. require_auth is opt-in, so forgetting it is the bug to hunt.

nodes.label: mock_auths
nodes.rationale: mock_all_auths approves everything and can hide a missing require_auth. Pair it with env.auths(), or approve one invocation with MockAuth and MockAuthInvoke. env.auths() is only the latest invocation and resets on the next client call, so assert immediately and check the exact tree on security-critical paths. Use mock_all_auths_allowing_non_root_auth() when the contract authorizes calls below the entry point.

nodes.label: Auth Trees
nodes.rationale: A user signs a tree of invocations, not one call. require_auth passes only if the path and arguments match the signed tree, and each node matches at most once. Auth does not cascade, and SDKs build the tree from simulation. Changing the call graph silently breaks signers of the old shape. Re-authorize at every layer that uses an address's authority. If deposit pulls tokens for a user without user.require_auth, anyone can consume a pre-signed inner transfer. That is the most common real-world auth bug. The host handles replay protection, so contracts do not track nonces.

nodes.label: L9. Relayer lock scope
nodes.rationale: The lock is released after sendTransaction and before inclusion, so a second job can reuse the sequence number and hit tx_bad_seq. The retry policy treats that as retryable, so it self-heals at the cost of wasted attempts. Suspected.

nodes.label: Settlement design
nodes.rationale: Unique nonce is the idempotency key. txHash and signedTxXdr are persisted before submit so a crash resumes instead of double-spending. The relayer lock uses a token-checked Lua release in a finally. BullMQ jobId is deterministic, retries are split from UnrecoverableError, and failed jobs are retained.

nodes.label: Idempotent queue jobs
nodes.rationale: A job can run more than once. Use a deterministic jobId, unique constraints, and status checks. Transient errors retry; permanent failures throw UnrecoverableError. Keep failed jobs for inspection.

nodes.label: Assume failure
nodes.rationale: Networks time out, Redis restarts, the same webhook arrives twice, and two requests race. The usual answers are idempotency keys, unique constraints, transactions, timeouts, and retries with backoff.

nodes.label: CAP-0038
nodes.rationale: Defines liquidity_pool_use_count. A trustline with that count above 0 cannot be deleted until the pool position is withdrawn.

nodes.label: Claimable Balances
nodes.rationale: A wallet display entry or a claimable balance is not a trustline. Remove claimable balances by claiming them or clawing them back, not with ChangeTrust.

nodes.label: Clawback
nodes.rationale: Issuer operation that pulls tokens back from an account. It requires AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED. Treat assets with clawback enabled cautiously.

nodes.label: Custom Contract Tokens
nodes.rationale: Last resort when SAC cannot express the behavior: complex transfer logic, custom authorization, non-standard tokens, custom DeFi integration, or NFTs and semi-fungible tokens. Royalties, fees, and transfer restrictions can often stay on a classic asset plus a SAC admin contract so DEX, anchors, wallets, and trustlines still work.

nodes.label: Friendbot
nodes.rationale: Testnet faucet at https://friendbot.stellar.org used to fund new accounts such as a separate issuer and distributor. Mainnet has no Friendbot.

nodes.label: Liquidity Pool Shares
nodes.rationale: Asset type that represents a liquidity-pool position. Withdraw the position and remove the pool-share trustline before deleting an asset trustline the pool still uses.

nodes.label: OpenZeppelin Stellar Contracts
nodes.rationale: Reference NFT implementations for SEP-50: Base, Consecutive, and Enumerable. Repository OpenZeppelin/stellar-contracts.

nodes.label: Stellar Asset Contract
nodes.rationale: SAC is the interop layer that exposes a classic asset to smart contracts as a SEP-41 token. The contract id is derived with Asset.contractId. Prefer a thin SAC admin that calls mint, burn, and clawback over a fully custom token when SAC can express the behavior. The admin starts as the issuer, and only the current admin can authorize the first set_admin, so call set_admin before locking the issuer. Locking first leaves the admin as the locked issuer forever. An unlocked issuer can mint outside the contract and bypass the role model.

nodes.label: SEP-0001
nodes.rationale: Publish asset metadata in /.well-known/stellar.toml under [[CURRENCIES]]. A missing home_domain or CURRENCIES entry is not evidence of a scam. Validate by issuer and SAC derivation, not by the presence of stellar.toml.

nodes.label: SEP-0010
nodes.rationale: Web authentication with a Stellar account: the server issues a challenge transaction, the client signs it with a wallet, and the server checks the signature.

nodes.label: SEP-0024
nodes.rationale: Hosted deposit and withdrawal for fiat on- and off-ramps. An interactive webview where the anchor handles KYC and the fiat transfer.

nodes.label: SEP-0045
nodes.rationale: Extends SEP-10 to contract accounts (C... addresses). Draft status. Required for smart-wallet and passkey-based anchor integrations; verify the current status before relying on it.

nodes.label: SEP-0050
nodes.rationale: Draft contract interface for NFTs on Stellar, with Base, Consecutive, and Enumerable reference implementations. Verify the current status before relying on it.

nodes.label: SEP-41
nodes.rationale: Standard contract token interface: balance, transfer, approve, allowance, decimals, name, and symbol. Classic issuance stays the default; SEP-41 contract tokens are the custom-logic alternative.

nodes.label: soroban-sdk
nodes.rationale: Rust contract SDK. A contract calls a SAC through soroban_sdk token::Client, which uses the standard token interface.

nodes.label: Stellar Assets (Classic)
nodes.rationale: Prefer classic assets over custom contract tokens unless custom logic is required. They are built in, cheaper than contract calls, and already work with wallets, exchanges, anchors, and the DEX order book. Use separate issuing and distribution accounts. For a fixed supply, lock the issuer by setting master weight to 0, because a payment from an unlocked issuer is a mint.

nodes.label: Trustlines
nodes.rationale: Credit assets require a trustline; native XLM does not. ChangeTrust with limit 0 deletes a trustline only when the balance is exactly 0, open DEX offers that create buying liabilities are cancelled, and no liquidity pool still references the asset. Match the asset by code and issuer. op_invalid_limit means balance or buying liabilities remain; op_cannot_delete means a pool still uses the trustline.

nodes.label: USDT0
nodes.rationale: Production classic asset USDT0:GATISXX6BZ6NC7IKQBY37CJD4SOZL3CYZJWXEDG6JVIY4WBS6KXJHN6Q whose SAC admin is a role-gated contract. The admin forwards mint, clawback, set_authorized, and set_admin. A cross-chain bridge holds only the minter role. It ships with no stellar.toml.

nodes.label: getLedgerEntries
nodes.rationale: Read a raw persistent contract-data ledger key only when that key is not exposed as a contract method. Decode the stored ScVal with scValToNative.

nodes.label: NotFoundError
nodes.rationale: Typed error from @stellar/stellar-sdk. horizon.loadAccount rejects with NotFoundError when the account is unfunded; treat that native balance as 0. Submission failures are different: Horizon returns result codes under error.response.data.extras.result_codes.

nodes.label: rpc.queryContract
nodes.rationale: One-call read of a contract method, including the built-in spec for Stellar Asset Contracts, with named args and no manual ScVal work. isReadCall false means the result is only a simulation of a state-changing call, which still has to be signed through contract.Client. getContractMethods lists the callable interface from the contract id.

nodes.label: Next.js App Router
nodes.rationale: Wallet and payment UI are client components. The root layout wraps children in a client Providers component. The connect button and send-payment form use the Freighter hook, then build, sign with the network passphrase, and submit.

nodes.label: contract.Client
nodes.rationale: Canonical JS way to call a Stellar contract. It reads the interface from the network so methods are called by name and return an AssembledTransaction. Preview is a free simulation; signAndSend submits and polls. Build ScVals by hand only on the low-level path. Use Contract.call plus prepareTransaction only when batching a contract call with classic operations. Multi-party auth uses needsNonInvokerSigningBy and signAuthEntries. Node scripts use contract.basicNodeSigner instead of a browser wallet.

nodes.label: Freighter
nodes.rationale: Primary browser wallet, via @stellar/freighter-api, which is not part of @stellar/stellar-sdk. getAddress stays empty until requestAccess has been granted; a non-empty address means the app is already authorized. Signing returns signed transaction XDR. Handle a missing extension, user rejection, and a wallet on the wrong network.

nodes.label: Horizon
nodes.rationale: Classic operation path via StellarSdk.Horizon.Server. Testnet is https://horizon-testnet.stellar.org and mainnet is https://horizon.stellar.org. Submit classic transactions here. Transactions that invoke a host function go to Soroban RPC instead.

nodes.label: Soroban RPC
nodes.rationale: RPC for smart-contract transactions, via StellarSdk.rpc.Server. Testnet public URL is https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org. Mainnet URL must be set from a provider in NEXT_PUBLIC_STELLAR_MAINNET_RPC_URL. sendTransaction plus pollTransaction replaces a hand-rolled poll. prepareTransaction simulates and applies footprint, auth, and fees.

nodes.label: @stellar/stellar-base
nodes.rationale: Former low-level package. As of stellar-sdk v16 it is folded into @stellar/stellar-sdk. Uninstall it and change imports over, because keeping both breaks instanceof checks.

nodes.label: Stellar dApp
nodes.rationale: Keep one SDK instance for Horizon, Soroban RPC, and transaction building, and split client and server in Next.js. Show signing and confirmation state, and block double submission. Mainnet RPC comes from an env-provided URL; testnet uses the public Horizon and Soroban endpoints.

nodes.label: @stellar/stellar-sdk
nodes.rationale: JavaScript SDK for browser and Node.js. v16 requires Node.js 22 or newer, is ESM-first, uses native fetch instead of axios, and folded @stellar/stellar-base into this package. Keeping the base package installed breaks instanceof checks. Wallet kits, passkey accounts, and the OpenZeppelin relayer are separate packages. Official docs also publish llms.txt bundles for agents.

nodes.label: Stellar Wallets Kit
nodes.rationale: Multi-wallet kit. v2 is a static singleton installed from JSR as @creit-tech/stellar-wallets-kit, not from the old npm scope @creit.tech/stellar-wallets-kit. init once, then authModal replaces v1 openModal. defaultModules loads wallets that need no extra setup; WalletConnect, Ledger, and Trezor must be added explicitly. npm updates are expected to stop. Not part of the JS SDK.

nodes.label: Wallet Standard
nodes.rationale: Named in the skill description alongside Freighter and Stellar Wallets Kit. This file does not describe the Wallet Standard API.

nodes.label: Launchtube
nodes.rationale: Deprecated fee-sponsorship service. OpenZeppelin Relayer replaces it and uses Stellar fee bumps instead.

nodes.label: LOBSTR
nodes.rationale: External wallet that Smart Account Kit can connect through an adapter, alongside Freighter.

nodes.label: OpenZeppelin Relayer
nodes.rationale: Also called Stellar Channels Service. Submits gasless transactions with Stellar's native fee bump so the user does not need XLM for fees. Replaces the deprecated Launchtube service. Client package is @openzeppelin/relayer-plugin-channels. Hosted testnet is https://channels.openzeppelin.com/testnet; production is self-hosted with Docker. Not part of the JS SDK.

nodes.label: OpenZeppelin Stellar Contracts
nodes.rationale: Audited account implementation Smart Account Kit builds on. Context rules and an auth digest live in OpenZeppelin/stellar-contracts. Reach for this kit when those rules, thresholds, or spending limits are required.

nodes.label: Passkey Kit
nodes.rationale: Sibling SDK to Smart Account Kit with a flat multi-signer Signatures map. Choose it when that flat model is enough. Not drop-in compatible with Smart Account Kit's context-rule accounts, and neither README deprecates the other.

nodes.label: Smart Account Kit
nodes.rationale: Passwordless smart wallets from the smart-account-kit package. Authorization is OpenZeppelin context rules plus an auth digest on the audited stellar-contracts account. Use it when you need context rules, thresholds, or spending limits. It is a sibling of Passkey Kit, not a newer version, and the two are not drop-in compatible. Neither project declares the other deprecated. Signers include WebAuthn passkeys (secp256r1), Ed25519 keys, and policies. Sessions restore from IndexedDB without a prompt.

nodes.label: WebAuthn
nodes.rationale: Passkey standard Smart Account Kit uses for passwordless authentication. The kit is configured with a WebAuthn verifier contract address.

nodes.label: Express
nodes.rationale: HTTP platform the Nest app is created on in src/main.ts. Middleware is applied there, in order, before bootstrap adds the global prefix and pipes.

nodes.label: NestJS
nodes.rationale: API in apps/backend. Feature code lives in src/modules/<feature>. Controllers own HTTP and call services; services own business logic and persistence. Do not call one controller from another. Register feature modules in src/app.module.ts. Routes are the global /api prefix plus controller and method paths; do not silently move existing paths. Use .js suffixes on relative imports where neighbors do. Preserve status codes, response shapes, and 405 handlers. Never print or commit .env values. When verifying, run the narrowest test and do not send real SMS, payments, or Stellar transactions unless asked. This skill is not for mobile or Soroban contract work.

nodes.label: Prisma
nodes.rationale: Database access goes through src/infra/prisma/prisma.service.ts. Runtime reads DATABASE_URL. Prisma CLI configuration is prisma.config.ts and prefers DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED when it is set, for migrations. npm run build generates the Prisma client.

nodes.label: @prisma/adapter-pg
nodes.rationale: Postgres driver adapter Prisma uses in this backend, wired through prisma.service.ts.

nodes.label: Redis
nodes.rationale: Redis access goes through the shared RedisService. Some backend end-to-end specs need Redis at 127.0.0.1:6379.

nodes.label: Stellar
nodes.rationale: Route tests must not submit real Stellar transactions unless a live operation was explicitly requested. Use mocks or validation-only requests. The focused unit suite covers wallet and settlement. This backend skill does not cover Soroban contract work.

nodes.label: Swagger
nodes.rationale: API docs configured from src/bootstrap.ts together with the /api prefix, CORS, and exception handling.

nodes.label: ValidationPipe
nodes.rationale: Strict global pipe configured in src/bootstrap.ts. It transforms values, does not silently drop unknown fields, and rejects non-whitelisted fields. Validate requests with DTOs through this pipe.

nodes.label: Issuer Authorization Flags
nodes.rationale: AUTH_REQUIRED means a trustline needs approval before the holder can receive tokens. AUTH_REVOCABLE lets the issuer freeze balances. AUTH_IMMUTABLE makes the flags permanent. AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED allows clawback. If revocable and clawback are both set, confirm the issuer master key weight is 0 and identify who holds the SAC admin roles before listing the asset. A contract admin does not remove the issuer's power while the master key can still sign.

nodes.rationale: Account loads and transaction submission go through Horizon. The examples use the testnet server.

nodes.label: Bitcoin SDK
nodes.rationale: Bitcoin SDKs are grouped with Stellar SDKs as Node-oriented libraries that need the same polyfills, with random values loaded first.

nodes.label: fast-text-encoding
nodes.rationale: TextEncoder polyfill for Node-oriented libraries. Keep the polyfill set minimal and ordered.

nodes.label: react-native-get-random-values

nodes.label: react-native-url-polyfill
nodes.rationale: URL polyfill for Node-oriented libraries. Load it with the other polyfills at the start of index.ts.

nodes.label: Stellar SDK
nodes.rationale: Stellar SDKs are Node-oriented and need crypto, buffer, URL, and TextEncoder polyfills loaded before they run. Expose that work through one service wrapper so a faster native implementation can replace it later.

nodes.label: AccountsModule
nodes.rationale: Register, users check, and users lookup. Register can require the OTP token when REQUIRE_OTP_TOKEN is set.

nodes.label: AnchorModule
nodes.rationale: Serves SEP-1 stellar.toml at the domain root and the SEP-24 anchor API under the global prefix. Interactive deposit and withdraw URLs are signed as separate 15-minute HS256 JWTs. Simulate-payment is testnet-only and uses a one-time Redis claim. Phase 6 is not ready to ship until the deferred web pages and remaining live database-backed parity checks are done.

nodes.label: AuthModule
nodes.rationale: GET /api/auth issues the SEP-10 challenge and POST /api/auth issues the JWT used by Sep10JwtGuard. PIN verify keeps the legacy Redis keys and the per-phone failure lock.

nodes.label: Ed25519SignatureGuard
nodes.rationale: Verifies canonical deposit, withdraw, and versioned online-transfer messages with strict Base64 signatures.

nodes.label: EngineModule
nodes.rationale: Soroban deposit, withdraw, online transfer, offline-key rotation, and recipient registry. Online transfer requires protocol v2. Settle runs as a BullMQ processor instead of a public QStash callback. Live testnet verification of every engine route is still pending.

nodes.label: engine-settlement queue
nodes.rationale: SMS and engine share SettlementQueueService, queue engine-settlement, and job process-offline-voucher. Nonce-cache markers are written only after a successful publish. Jobs already buffered in the obsolete pijin-settlements queue are not migrated automatically.

nodes.label: OtpModule
nodes.rationale: Send and verify OTP, including OTP_TEST_MODE and test numbers. Verify issues an OTP verification JWT. The live OTP flow stayed blocked when test-mode confirmation and probe variables were absent.

nodes.label: SMS_DISPATCH_SECRET
nodes.rationale: QStash signatures go away with the queue migration. The header x-sms-dispatch-secret protects POST /api/sms/dispatch while callers still use HTTP, and the route stays unavailable when the secret is unset. BullMQ delivery is the preferred internal path.

nodes.label: StellarModule
nodes.rationale: Wraps @stellar/stellar-sdk, Horizon and Soroban RPC clients, and the pijin_core contract client. After the Phase 4 cleanup it provides StellarService only.

nodes.label: TextBee
nodes.rationale: SMS gateway for OTP and inbound vouchers, with a primary device and a fallback device. The free plan allows only one active device, so fallback delivery is still unverified.

nodes.label: TextbeeSignatureGuard
nodes.rationale: POST /api/sms/webhook reads a bounded raw body and checks TextBee HMAC-SHA256 with TEXTBEE_WEBHOOK_SECRET from x-signature or x-textbee-signature before parsing the voucher.

nodes.label: /api/engine/settle
nodes.rationale: QStash settlement worker with a 64 KB body ceiling and an upstash-signature check. A Prisma unique nonce returns DUPLICATE_SKIPPED for a completed settlement. A local Ed25519 check against the registered offline device key aborts bad vouchers before relayer fees. Non-retryable failures notify the sender by SMS.

nodes.label: Upstash QStash
nodes.rationale: Serverless queue between the SMS webhook and the settlement worker. Retryable handler responses are retried by QStash; permanent failures return HTTP 200 so the retry loop stops.

nodes.label: /api/sms/webhook
nodes.rationale: Ingress gateway. Authenticates Textbee before business logic, drops MESSAGE_SENT delivery receipts, caps SMS at 300 characters, allows 3 requests per 60 seconds per sender phone, and fail-opens a 24-hour Redis nonce check. The eager processing SMS was removed so QStash would not double-text the user. Preview deployments resolve the settlement URL from the Host header, falling back to NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL.

nodes.label: Soroban
nodes.rationale: Stellar Soroban contract calls are the expensive end of the pipeline. Malformed input is rejected before RPC execution or transaction fees.

nodes.label: TEXTBEE_WEBHOOK_SECRET
nodes.rationale: Shared HMAC secret. Verification fails closed in production when it is unset.

nodes.label: Deferred web pages
nodes.rationale: SEP-24 deposit and withdraw pages are required before Phase 6 can ship. Privacy policy and delete-account pages are likely required by app stores. Whether Nest server-rendered views or a separate small web app serves them is undecided.

nodes.label: Settlement retry classifier
nodes.rationale: The producer keeps five attempts with exponential backoff, and permanent worker errors stay unrecoverable. Phase 4 ports engine-retry-classifier.test.ts. A hosted Redis probe completed an isolated BullMQ job, but the app engine-settlement worker and its retry schedule were not exercised. BullMQ warned that the Redis eviction policy is volatile-* and noeviction is preferred.

nodes.label: SEP-10 memo preservation
nodes.rationale: Ignore the GET memo parameter, but keep a memo claim when a valid POST challenge includes one. Legacy passes the GET memo where the Stellar SDK ignores it, while POST extracts and conditionally emits the challenge memo. Issuer validation stays aligned with the first SEP10_HOME_DOMAINS entry and sub must be a non-empty string.

nodes.label: isRetryableSettlementError
nodes.rationale: Retryable faults return true and HTTP 500 so QStash retries: HTTP 429, 502, 503, 504, network drops, and Stellar tx_bad_seq or tx_insufficient_fee. Permanent faults return false and HTTP 200 with status FAILED: Soroban contract errors, invalid Ed25519 signatures, account or token misses, and corrupted vouchers. That stops the retry loop.

nodes.label: normalizeSettlementUserFailure
nodes.rationale: Operator logs keep a sanitized root cause on Settlement.failReason. User SMS gets short copy such as insufficient balance or an already-used voucher, without contract codes or stack traces. A raw internal stack trace yields an empty string so a safe fallback is used. sendSms failures are caught so a telecom error cannot change the QStash status code.

nodes.label: parseOfflineVoucher
nodes.rationale: Zero-trust parse of tokenId:senderShortId:receiverShortId:amountBase62:nonce:signature. Requires exactly six parts, 6-character Base62 short ids, a 32-byte nonce, a 64-byte Ed25519 signature, a positive amount, and an amount no higher than the Soroban i128 maximum.

nodes.label: readBoundedRequestBody
nodes.rationale: Reads the request stream once with a hard ceiling: 2048 bytes for webhooks and 65536 bytes for settlement. Rejects early from Content-Length and aborts if the stream exceeds the ceiling, so HMAC can use cached raw bytes without re-reading the body.

nodes.label: verifyQStashSignature
nodes.rationale: Wraps the Upstash QStash Receiver over the pre-read raw body. A missing or invalid signature returns valid false instead of throwing HTTP 500, so the route can respond 401 or 403.

nodes.label: verifyTextbeeHmac
nodes.rationale: Constant-time HMAC-SHA256 using crypto.timingSafeEqual, so timing side channels do not leak the secret. Accepts a sha256= prefix, raw hex, and Base64 digests. Implemented in apps/backend/lib/sms-security.ts.

nodes.label: verifyTimestampDrift
nodes.rationale: Checks x-timestamp or x-textbee-timestamp inside a plus or minus 300 second window. Accepts 10-digit seconds and 13-digit milliseconds. Passes when the header is absent, and enforces drift when it is present.

nodes.label: Managed Better Auth
nodes.rationale: One of three identity choices that live in the neon-auth skill, beside keeping an existing IdP or pointing at self-managed Better Auth. Do not install that skill with neon skills -s neon-auth until the released CLI catalog includes the name; unknown names fail. Fetch the skill docs, or the same files from the agent-skills repo if the docs URL is unpublished.

nodes.label: Self-Managed Better Auth
nodes.rationale: Use when a required feature is outside Managed Better Auth support. The self-managed document is a pointer, not a second tutorial.

nodes.label: Claimable Neon
nodes.rationale: Provisions a temporary project before a human creates an account. The agent holds an identity assertion, not a Neon API key, and neon claim refuses --api-key and --profile. Postgres is always granted. Auth and the Data API are granted when requested. Functions, Object Storage, and the AI Gateway return granted false with reason requires_claim; report those denied capabilities and do not retry or strip them. The project is created in aws-us-east-2 unless --region-id is set, and the region cannot change after create. Do not mint a claim URL until the human is ready. Opening the URL does not freeze access. Continuing to Neon rotates DATABASE_URL and revokes existing access tokens. A claim code lasts expires_in (15 minutes, 900 seconds, today); each mint cancels the previous unused code. When reconciled is true, the pre-claim DATABASE_URL no longer works. External JWKS is accepted only after claim. An agent must not complete the claim. Only invalid_grant, project_expired, and project_claimed mean the stored identity assertion is dead; token_expired means re-exchange it. The claimable resource is /v1/projects/{id}, not /v1/databases/{id}. Unclaimed projects expire at project_expires_at (72 hours today), independent of the claim-code clock.

nodes.label: Function Trigger
nodes.rationale: A branch-scoped rule that POSTs to a Neon Function on a cron (type schedule) or when an object is created in a bucket (type storage_object_created). Same regions as Functions. Prefer a triggers map in neon.ts; the record key is the trigger name, and neon deploy applies triggers after the functions they target. Names must be unique among every trigger visible on the branch. Remote triggers omitted from neon.ts are left alone; delete them with neon triggers delete. Needs Neon CLI 4.21 or newer and @neon/config 1.7.0. CLI create takes --cron or --bucket, not both. Without --branch, get, update, enable, disable, and delete treat the trigger id as a branch name. Inherited triggers, created on a parent branch, show Inherited true on the child and start disabled. Deploying a neon.ts that declares the same trigger enables that copy; omit it to leave the inherited trigger disabled.

nodes.label: parseTriggerDelivery
nodes.rationale: Authenticates a trigger delivery. Import it from @neon/functions version 0.11.0 or newer. parseTrigger and parseTriggerInvocation stay schedule-only. The full payload and Hono example live in the neon-functions skill.

nodes.label: Loki-compatible read API
nodes.rationale: Read-only HTTP subset for branch logs, authenticated with a Neon API key bearer token. It is not a push endpoint or a complete Loki deployment. query_range supports LogQL stream selectors and line filters, plus since or start/end, limit, and direction. It does not support aggregations, parsers, or formatting stages. A Grafana data source appends /loki/api/v1 to the URL it is given, so confirm that data-source URL against the Neon docs instead of pasting the console base unchanged.

nodes.label: Neon Logs
nodes.rationale: Branch-scoped logs. Today only Neon Functions and Object Storage emit records. Postgres compute and the AI Gateway do not yet. A branch that cannot serve logs returns 404 with reason telemetry_not_enabled; an enabled branch with no rows in the window returns 200 empty; an unknown branch returns reason branch_not_found. Query the branch that hosts the deployed function or bucket. Without --branch the CLI uses the branch pinned in .neon, or the project default, so an empty result is often the wrong branch. The window defaults to 1 hour on query and 6 hours on field-values and cannot exceed 7 days. --source accepts pg_endpoint, but that source stays empty until Postgres logs ship. If --minimum-severity is unsupported, use a case-sensitive --severity-text match. LogQL uses the stream label entity_type, not source. Prefer Neon CLI 3.1 or newer, then the MCP read-only log tools. In @neon/sdk, query is a lazy paginated iterable that throws on error, while fields and fieldValues follow throwOnError, which defaults to false. fieldValues can set is_truncated, in which case values are an arbitrary subset.
nodes.source_location: Logs: CLI, Loki, and SDK pagination

nodes.label: parseEnv
nodes.rationale: @neon/env validates process env against the services declared in neon.ts and returns a typed object. By default every variable the config implies is required. Pass a list of keys to require only a subset: autocomplete offers only variables the config enables, and unselected variables are neither enforced nor present. Use that when an app needs DATABASE_URL but not DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED.

nodes.label: @neon/sdk
nodes.rationale: Official TypeScript client for the Neon API. Fetch-based, zero-dependency, and ESM-only, generated from the OpenAPI spec with an ergonomic layer on top. New code should prefer it for projects, branches, and snapshots in dev scripts, CI, and platforms. It succeeds @neondatabase/api-client. The older client is not deprecated and is safe to keep. Log query pagination is documented with the Loki logs reference.

nodes.label: @neondatabase/api-client
nodes.rationale: Earlier Neon API client. Axios-based and generated-only. It is not deprecated and is safe to keep using, but new code should prefer @neon/sdk.

nodes.label: AI Gateway
nodes.rationale: One API for frontier and open-source models, supporting chat completions and responses, powered by Databricks Unity AI Gateway. Declare aiGateway in neon.ts to request gateway env vars. Without neon.ts, a bare neon env pull includes the default gateway credential on claimed projects, but the implicit pulls inside link, checkout, and apply do not pull an undeclared gateway token. Same four AWS regions as Functions. Model routing is the neon-ai-gateway skill. On an unclaimed Claimable project the gateway is denied until a human claims it.

nodes.label: Better Auth
nodes.rationale: Keep a working Better Auth install. Neon Auth is the managed form; use it when there is no provider yet or the user asks to migrate login.

nodes.label: Claimable Neon
nodes.rationale: The no-account path, including neon.new, Claimable Postgres, claimable.neon.tech, instant Postgres, and a no-signup database. Do not create a Claimable project as a substitute when an existing account fails to authenticate; stop and ask the user to sign in. Do not run neon init --agent or neon auth on this path. Unclaimed projects expire at project_expires_at (72 hours today). Claim codes expire in expires_in (15 minutes today). Functions, Object Storage, and the AI Gateway report requires_claim until a human claims the project. Add Auth with neon.ts and neon deploy when login is requested and no existing provider should be kept.

nodes.label: Clerk
nodes.rationale: Keep Clerk. Use neon-auth only if the user asks to migrate login.

nodes.label: Data API
nodes.rationale: Optional PostgREST-compatible HTTP interface. Use it only when the app already uses PostgREST or a supabase-js database client, or is migrating that client. There is no neon-data-api skill; configuration is dataApi in neon.ts. New apps should query Postgres from Functions or existing handlers. Putting PostgREST in the browser and relying on RLS is easy to get wrong because a misconfigured policy exposes the database. The default authProvider is neon, so enabling dataApi alone is a type error until Auth is enabled or authProvider is external with a JWKS URL. Do not enable Auth only to silence that error in an app that never needed the Data API. A Supabase package used only for Auth or Storage is not a database-client dependency. It is a compatibility toggle, not part of a default backend.

nodes.label: Databricks
nodes.rationale: The other way to reach the same Lakebase Postgres infrastructure, features, and engineering team, alongside the rest of the Databricks suite. Call the database Lakebase Postgres. Neon is the brand and the Neon access path.

nodes.label: Databricks Unity AI Gateway
nodes.rationale: The Databricks service that powers the Neon AI Gateway.

nodes.label: Lakebase Postgres
nodes.rationale: The database itself, one product reached through Neon (free plan plus the other backend primitives) or through Databricks, with the same infrastructure, features, and engineering team. The lakebase architecture is OLTP directly on cloud object storage, with storage decoupled from compute. Every project ships with it. New projects are created in AWS regions, and application traffic should use a pooled DATABASE_URL. A supplied DATABASE_URL with no Neon credentials is schema work for the neon-postgres skill and should be finished without provisioning.

nodes.label: Neon
nodes.rationale: Neon is the brand and access path for a set of cloud backend primitives around Lakebase Postgres, not the name of the database. Agents pick it for instant Postgres provision, copy-on-write branches and snapshots, compute that scales to zero while storage is still billed, and ordinary Postgres that works with any driver or ORM. Keep a working Better Auth, Clerk, Supabase Auth, S3, or supplied DATABASE_URL unless the user asks to replace it. Prefer the CLI over the MCP server unless the CLI is unavailable, blocked, or unauthenticated.

nodes.label: Neon Agent Program
nodes.rationale: Enroll only when the work is a fleet of user databases, such as app-generating agents and platforms. A single-app backend skips this. The program page covers instant provision, snapshots, scale-to-zero compute with storage still billed, Auth, and Data API compatibility. Guidance for platforms that operate Lakebase Postgres on Neon at scale is the neon-postgres-agent-platforms skill in the separate neondatabase/neon-for-agent-platforms repo.

nodes.label: Neon Auth
nodes.rationale: Managed Better Auth with users and sessions stored in Postgres. Use the neon-auth skill when login, users, and sessions have no existing provider. Keep existing Better Auth, Clerk, or Supabase Auth unless the user asks to migrate; a Supabase Auth migration keeps SupabaseAuthAdapter call shapes. Auth cannot be enabled on a project that uses IP Allow or Private Networking. neon-auth is absent from the current CLI skill catalog, so do not run neon skills -s neon-auth. Selecting data-api also declares Auth because the default Data API provider requires it.

nodes.label: Neon Branch
nodes.rationale: An isolated copy-on-write clone of the data, taken from the current state or from a past state inside the project's retained history window. It shares data with its parent until writes diverge, and those writes are stored independently as deltas. It can be modified or deleted freely. Create one whenever you would create a git branch. neon checkout applies neon.ts only while creating a branch; checking out an existing branch does not reconcile it.

nodes.label: Neon CLI
nodes.rationale: Preferred over the MCP server because it can deploy Neon Functions and drive link, checkout, and neon.ts. Do not run neon login or neon auth unattended, and do not launch browser authentication for an unattended agent. Authenticated neon init writes neon.ts in place and does not deploy or wire the app. If init already installed the Neon plugin, do not also run neon mcp and neon skills for the same agent. link and checkout pull env by default; pass --no-env-pull when a supplied DATABASE_URL or AWS_* value must stay. init has no --no-env-pull flag.

nodes.label: Neon Functions
nodes.rationale: Long-running serverless compute close to the database for WebSocket servers, server-sent events, APIs, and long agent HTTP streams. A function must start returning a response within 15 minutes, and a quiet stream must send at least one byte every 15 minutes. Public HTTPS URLs must verify a JWT or API key before accessing data. For long agent or image streams, mint a JWT on the app server and have the client call the function directly. New HTTP APIs belong here, or in an existing handler, rather than in browser-facing PostgREST. Same four AWS regions as Object Storage, the AI Gateway, and Realtime. Authentication and runtime limits are in the neon-functions skill.

nodes.label: Neon MCP Server
nodes.rationale: Fallback when the CLI is unavailable, blocked, unauthenticated, or the user prefers it. One global install serves every project. Without --oauth it writes an API key into the agent user config. A project-level install must use OAuth so no key lands in a file git can commit. Always pass --agent; with -y and no --agent, the command writes to every installed agent.

nodes.label: neon.ts
nodes.rationale: Branch config and infrastructure-as-code, written with defineConfig from @neon/config. It declares which services a branch should have and types the env vars those services imply. Empty functions or buckets maps are configuration slots, not a deployed API. Do not replace an existing neon.ts wholesale. Invalid combinations fail TypeScript compilation, and the error names the valid fix. neon deploy, an alias of neon config apply, provisions the declaration and then pulls env into the local env file. Never coerce a missing process.env value to an empty string: that uploads an empty value and deletes the live key. An empty KEY= assignment is also empty.

nodes.label: Object Storage
nodes.rationale: S3-compatible object storage that branches with the project. Keep an existing S3 or other object store unless the user asks to replace it. A public_read bucket can serve prototype pages, but there is no website mode (PutBucketWebsite returns 501), no SPA fallbacks, no custom domains, and no CDN, so every page view is egress. Available only in aws-us-east-2, aws-us-east-1, aws-eu-central-1, and aws-ap-southeast-1. Bucket setup lives in the neon-object-storage skill.

nodes.label: PostgREST
nodes.rationale: The Data API is the compatibility path for an existing PostgREST client or a supabase-js database client. Browser PostgREST with RLS is a poor fit for a new app because a bad policy exposes the database. Generic REST endpoints should be a Function or an existing handler.

nodes.label: Realtime
nodes.rationale: Beta. Makes any SQL query live: type-safe live queries and optimistic mutations against Lakebase Postgres for reactive apps and agents. Declare it as preview.realtime in neon.ts. It is not available on a Claimable project until that project is claimed. Same four AWS regions as Functions. Setup, sealed queries, and client bindings are the neon-realtime skill.

nodes.label: S3
nodes.rationale: Keep a working S3 or other object store. Neon Object Storage is the S3-compatible choice when the app has no object store yet.

nodes.label: Supabase Auth
nodes.rationale: Keep Supabase Auth unless the user asks to migrate. A migration uses Managed Better Auth and keeps SupabaseAuthAdapter call shapes. A Supabase package used only for Auth or Storage does not establish a database-client dependency.

nodes.label: Upstash QStash
nodes.rationale: Neon has no built-in message queue. Use Upstash QStash for background jobs, queues, retries, and delayed delivery to a Function, and keep any queue the app already uses. Cron and custom HTTP, WebSocket, or SSE work belong on Functions.

nodes.label: Upstash Redis
nodes.rationale: Neon has no built-in key-value store. Pair it with Upstash Redis for caching hot reads and rate limits, and keep any Redis the app already uses.

nodes.label: Branch-First Dev Flow
nodes.rationale: Recommended day-to-day loop when using Neon services. neon.ts declares what every branch should have, and checkout is how you move between those branches. Each half works on its own, and they compose. link and checkout pull the branch env by default, so DATABASE_URL lands in the local env file. Pass --no-env-pull and use neon-env run, neon-env export, fetchEnv, or neon dev when secrets should not be written to disk. Checking out an existing branch does not apply neon.ts; use neon deploy --env for that.

nodes.label: AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED
nodes.rationale: Lets the issuer claw back tokens. Operation.clawback requires this flag.

nodes.label: AUTH_IMMUTABLE
nodes.rationale: Makes issuer flags permanent.

nodes.label: AUTH_REQUIRED
nodes.rationale: Users must be approved before they can receive the asset.

nodes.label: AUTH_REVOCABLE
nodes.rationale: Lets the issuer freeze trustlines. When this flag and clawback are both set, confirm the issuer master key weight is 0 and identify who holds the SAC admin roles before listing the asset.

nodes.label: CAP-0038
nodes.rationale: An asset trustline with liquidity_pool_use_count greater than 0 cannot be deleted.

nodes.label: ChangeTrust
nodes.rationale: A positive limit creates a trustline and limit 0 deletes it. Removal fails with op_invalid_limit when balance or buying liabilities remain, and op_cannot_delete when a liquidity pool still uses the asset.

nodes.label: Clawback
nodes.rationale: The issuer pulls tokens back from an account. This requires AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED. A SAC admin can also forward clawback.

nodes.label: Contract Tokens
nodes.rationale: Use a custom SEP-41 contract only when the SAC cannot express the behavior: complex transfer logic, custom authorization, non-standard tokens, custom DeFi integration, or NFTs and semi-fungible tokens. A fully custom token is a last resort.

nodes.label: Credit Asset
nodes.rationale: Issued by an account and identified by code plus issuer. Requires a trustline. Codes are 1-12 alphanumeric characters (credit_alphanum4 or credit_alphanum12). Validate the issuer, not just the code.

nodes.label: dapp skill
nodes.rationale: UI flows for trustline creation and asset display live in the dapp skill.

nodes.label: data skill
nodes.rationale: Looking up balances and trustline state is delegated to the data skill.

nodes.label: DEX
nodes.rationale: Classic assets integrate with the order-book DEX. That compatibility is a reason to stay on a Stellar asset plus a SAC admin instead of a custom token.

nodes.label: Distribution Account
nodes.rationale: The distributor opens a trustline, then receives the issued supply, so the issuer can be locked after distribution.

nodes.label: Issuing Account
nodes.rationale: Keep the issuing account separate from distribution. Payments from the issuer are minting. Consider multisig for the issuer.

nodes.label: Liquidity Pool Shares
nodes.rationale: Represent liquidity-pool positions. A trustline with liquidity_pool_use_count greater than 0 cannot be deleted until the position is withdrawn and the pool-share trustline is removed.

nodes.label: Stellar Asset Contract
nodes.rationale: SAC is the smart-contract interface for an existing classic asset. Use it inside a contract or DeFi protocol. Royalties, fees, and transfer restrictions can often be a normal issued asset plus a thin SAC admin contract instead of a fully custom token.

nodes.label: SAC Admin
nodes.rationale: A thin contract can drive SAC mint, burn, and clawback and keep classic ecosystem compatibility. USDT0's admin forwards mint, clawback, set_authorized, and set_admin. Call set_admin before locking the issuer: the admin starts as the issuer, and only the current admin can hand it over. Locking first leaves the admin stuck as the locked issuer.

nodes.label: SEP-0001
nodes.rationale: Publish asset metadata in the domain's /.well-known/stellar.toml under CURRENCIES.

nodes.label: SEP-0050
nodes.rationale: Standard contract interface for NFTs. Draft; verify current status. OpenZeppelin Stellar Contracts provide Base, Consecutive, and Enumerable reference implementations.

nodes.label: SEP-41
nodes.rationale: Contract-token standard. The SAC interface is balance, transfer, approve, allowance, decimals, name, and symbol.

nodes.label: SEP-7
nodes.rationale: Named with SEP-41 as a token-related SEP whose details live in the standards skill. This file does not describe SEP-7 further.

nodes.label: set_admin
nodes.rationale: Hands SAC admin from the issuer account to a contract. It must run while the issuer can still sign, before master weight is set to 0.

nodes.label: smart-contracts skill
nodes.rationale: Use the smart-contracts skill when classic assets are not enough and a custom token contract is required.

nodes.label: standards skill
nodes.rationale: Token-related SEPs, named as SEP-41, SEP-7, and others, are looked up in the standards skill.

nodes.label: Stellar Assets (Classic)
nodes.rationale: Prefer classic Stellar assets over custom contract tokens unless custom logic is required. They are built in, cheaper than contract calls, and have wallet, exchange, and order-book DEX support, plus freeze and clawback for compliance.

nodes.label: stellar.toml
nodes.rationale: A missing home_domain or CURRENCIES entry is not evidence of a scam. USDT0 ships without a stellar.toml. Validate by issuer and SAC derivation.

nodes.label: TokenClient
nodes.rationale: soroban_sdk TokenClient calls the SEP-41 interface on the SAC address. The example transfers after require_auth.

nodes.label: Trustlines
nodes.rationale: A credit asset requires a trustline. ChangeTrust with limit 0 deletes one only when the balance is exactly 0, buying liabilities are cleared, and no liquidity pool still uses the asset. Claimable balances and wallet-display entries are not trustlines.

nodes.label: USDT0
nodes.rationale: Production classic asset USDT0:GATISXX6BZ6NC7IKQBY37CJD4SOZL3CYZJWXEDG6JVIY4WBS6KXJHN6Q. Its SAC admin is a role-gated contract, a cross-chain bridge holds only the minter role, and it ships with no stellar.toml.

nodes.label: XLM
nodes.rationale: Stellar's native currency. No trustline is required.

nodes.label: layerzero.md
nodes.rationale: The USDT0 cross-chain deployment, where the bridge holds only the minter role, is documented in cross-chain/layerzero.md.

nodes.label: Lock Issuer
nodes.rationale: Set master weight to 0 so the issuer can never sign again. For a fixed supply, lock after distribution. For a SAC admin, an unlocked issuer can still mint by paying from the issuer account and bypass the contract roles. Lock only after set_admin.

nodes.label: Pools and AMMs
nodes.rationale: Define the invariant and fee accounting precisely, and slippage-check every user-facing swap.

nodes.label: contractimport
nodes.rationale: Import another contract's WASM to get a typed client. Callee errors abort the caller unless the call goes through a try_ client method.

nodes.label: extend_ttl_with_limits
nodes.rationale: Protocol 26 added extend_ttl_with_limits for persistent and instance storage so callers cannot force arbitrary rent. Arguments are extend_to, min_extension, and max_extension.

nodes.label: i128
nodes.rationale: i128 is the canonical SEP-41 token amount. It allows negatives, so reject amount < 0 on inputs.

nodes.label: invoke_contract
nodes.rationale: env.invoke_contract is the untyped dynamic call when the interface is not known at compile time.

nodes.label: Classic Issuer Flags
nodes.rationale: AUTH_REQUIRED, freezes via AUTH_REVOCABLE, and clawback apply to SAC transfers. A protocol that accepts arbitrary token addresses has to survive them.

nodes.label: MuxedAddress
nodes.rationale: MuxedAddress distinguishes sub-accounts of one address for exchanges and custodians. transfer accepts it as the destination, and a plain Address converts into it.

nodes.label: Protocol 26
nodes.rationale: Protocol 26 added bounded TTL extension, checked U256/I256 math, and SAC trust.

nodes.label: Stellar Asset Contract
nodes.rationale: Every classic Stellar asset exposes SEP-41 through its SAC, so a token address may be a custom contract, a wrapped classic asset, or native XLM. G-address balances live in trustlines (64-bit cap; missing or unauthorized trustline fails the transfer). C-address balances live in contract storage at full i128 range. Transfers to the issuer burn; transfers from the issuer mint.

nodes.label: SEP-0011
nodes.rationale: The SAC adds the SEP-0011 asset string (CODE:ISSUER or native) as a trailing topic on the standard token events.

nodes.label: SEP-41
nodes.rationale: SEP-41 is the token interface. transfer, approve, and burn authorize from; transfer_from and burn_from authorize the spender. Reads need no auth. mint, clawback, set_admin, set_authorized, and trust are SAC admin operations, not SEP-41.

nodes.label: StellarAssetClient
nodes.rationale: Admin client for a SAC: mint, clawback, set_admin, set_authorized, and trust (protocol 26+).

nodes.label: TokenClient
nodes.rationale: SDK client for the standard token interface, including every Stellar asset through its SAC, so no WASM import is needed. There is no msg.sender: pass the acting Address and require_auth it.

nodes.label: U256 and I256
nodes.rationale: 256-bit math uses U256 and I256. checked_add, sub, mul, pow, div, rem_euclid, shl, and shr return Option. Available in protocol 26 and later.

nodes.label: Vaults
nodes.rationale: Track total_assets and total_shares, round conservatively on mint and redeem, and include pause controls.

nodes.label: Check-then-act Races
nodes.rationale: State can change between transactions. Do the check and the write in one invocation, and take a slippage bound (min_out) from the caller. approve overwrites, so reducing a non-zero allowance can be front-run. Approve to 0 first, or use exact-amount auth.

nodes.label: Emergency Pause
nodes.rationale: Value-bearing contracts need pause controls and an incident runbook.

nodes.label: Integer Overflow
nodes.rationale: overflow-checks = true panics on overflow in the release profile, but checked math fails cleaner and survives a profile mistake. An unchecked negative i128 transfer withdraws from the destination. Use checked_* for 256-bit types (protocol 26+).

nodes.label: Assets Skill
nodes.rationale: Asset issuance, trustlines, and SAC deployment are covered by the assets skill.

nodes.label: Cross-Contract Tests
nodes.rationale: Register a real dependency from its WASM with contractimport and env.register(token::WASM), then drive both contracts through typed clients.

nodes.label: Token Allowances
nodes.rationale: approve(from, spender, amount, expiration_ledger) expires. The convention is temporary storage keyed by (from, spender) with TTL matching the expiration. Re-approving overwrites, so a spender can front-run a reduction and spend the old amount plus the new one. Approve to 0 first, or use exact-amount auth instead of a standing allowance.

nodes.label: Token-Consumer Review
nodes.rationale: A contract that takes a token address must assume native XLM's SAC, a wrapped classic asset's SAC, or a custom contract. Decide allowlist versus permissionless. Store decimals at registration; never assume 7. Re-check the amount received when a token can deliver less than requested. Survive missing trustlines, AUTH_REQUIRED, frozen accounts, and clawback. transfer_from authorizes the spender, not from. Emit the standard token events.

nodes.label: Address
nodes.rationale: There is no msg.sender. Pass the acting Address explicitly and require_auth it. require_auth on a user-supplied who proves control of who, not that who is allowed to act. Privileged paths must load the admin from storage and authorize that address.

nodes.label: Auth Trees
nodes.rationale: A user signs a tree of invocations, not a single call. require_auth deeper in the stack passes only if the path and arguments match the signed tree, and each tree node matches at most once. Auth does not cascade, so authorizing A.foo does not let every contract A calls claim that auth. Refactoring the call graph changes the tree and silently breaks signers of the old shape. SDKs build the tree from simulation. The most common real-world bug is failing to re-auth at every layer that uses an address's authority.

nodes.label: Authorization
nodes.rationale: Authorization is host-mediated and explicit. Require it when a call spends, reduces, reconfigures, or consumes an address's authority downstream. Reading public data and crediting a balance need no auth.

nodes.label: authorize_as_current_contract
nodes.rationale: When contract A directly calls B, B may require_auth A's address; the direct call authorizes only that immediate invocation. If B will make a deeper call that needs A's auth, A must pre-authorize it with authorize_as_current_contract.

nodes.label: Cross-contract Calls
nodes.rationale: Callee errors abort the caller unless the call uses try_ client methods. There is no msg.sender: pass the acting Address and require_auth it.

nodes.label: DeFi Patterns
nodes.rationale: Vaults should track total assets and shares, round conservatively on mint and redeem, and include pause controls. AMMs must define the invariant and fee accounting and slippage-check every user-facing swap. Oracles need freshness bounds, multi-source or median feeds, and circuit breakers. Regulated tokens should isolate allowlist, denylist, freeze, and forced-transfer logic in dedicated entrypoints with strong auth, emit policy-decision events, and never store PII on-chain.

nodes.label: invoke_contract
nodes.rationale: env.invoke_contract is the untyped dynamic call for an interface that is not known at compile time.

nodes.label: require_auth
nodes.rationale: require_auth asks whether that address authorized this contract, this function, and these exact arguments in this transaction. The host supplies replay protection with nonces and expiration, so contracts do not track nonces. Stellar accounts satisfy auth at their medium threshold.

nodes.label: require_auth_for_args
nodes.rationale: require_auth_for_args narrows the signed payload to the arguments you pass. That supports partial commitments, such as signing a max amount while the contract enforces actual <= max.

nodes.label: Authorization
nodes.rationale: require_auth is opt-in, so forgetting it is the failure mode to hunt for. The right address is the one with policy authority loaded from storage, not a caller-supplied parameter.

nodes.label: Host-managed Auth Replay Protection
nodes.rationale: Nonces and expirations on authorization entries are enforced by the host, not by contract code.

nodes.label: OpenZeppelin Security Detectors
nodes.rationale: The OpenZeppelin Soroban security detectors SDK includes auth_missing, unchecked_ft_transfer, and improper TTL extension, plus a framework for custom detectors.

nodes.label: Authorization Testing
nodes.rationale: mock_all_auths approves everything and can hide a missing require_auth. Pair it with env.auths() assertions or mock one invocation. Assert the exact tree, including sub-invocations, on security-critical paths. If the contract authorizes calls below the entry point, use mock_all_auths_allowing_non_root_auth.

nodes.label: env.auths
nodes.rationale: env.auths() returns (Address, AuthorizedInvocation) pairs for the most recent invocation only. Any later client call, even a read, resets it, so the assertion must run immediately.

nodes.label: mock_all_auths
nodes.rationale: mock_all_auths approves every authorization and can hide a missing require_auth.

nodes.label: mock_auths
nodes.rationale: mock_auths approves only the listed invocation: address, contract, function name, arguments, and sub-invokes.

nodes.label: Auth Replay Through Middleware
nodes.rationale: If a user has pre-signed an auth tree that includes an inner token.transfer, anyone can call a middleware entrypoint that never itself authorizes the user and consume that signature. Re-authorize at every layer that exercises an address's authority. This is the most common real-world auth bug.

nodes.label: Missing Authorization
nodes.rationale: Every privileged path needs require_auth on the address that holds policy authority. require_auth on an arbitrary caller-supplied address proves control of that address and nothing about permission.

nodes.label: Review severity guide
nodes.rationale: Critical is data loss, money loss, auth bypass, secret exposure, or an outage on deploy. High is a likely bug or exploitable weakness. Medium has a workaround or shows up only in unusual conditions. Low is style, naming, and small cleanup.

Each animation file targets at most 150 KB, the mascot at most 300 KB, and all animation assets at most 1 MB. Load clips per screen, not at startup. Avoid expo-blur on Android 8-10. Skia is not adopted. The Glass darkmode effect is out of scope because there is no dark mode.
